decisions.reason: Selecting Satin Reflection does not alter which wordmark elements receive champagne gold; the separate distribution choice is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The finish selection applies to material treatment and explicitly preserves the existing geometry rather than changing the Hero V construction.

The kerning refinement is a separate decision in the same message and is already represented by the candidate's same-message failure and MODIFY events; selecting Satin Reflection does not itself change spacing.
The new kerning-study proof format is separately and completely represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the selected finish does not require an additional proof-format state change.
Choosing a material finish does not change the E and L geometry, architectural vocabulary, proportions, or scale.
Applying Satin Reflection to the second V's right arm does not alter the second V's optical construction, design DNA, or right-arm geometry.
Applying the selected finish to the É accent does not change its required literal derivation from the Hero V terminal.
The Satin Reflection selection has no effect on the established all-caps case treatment.
The finish and color-placement selection does not change the second V's height relationship to the E, L, Hero V, or É accent.
The source selects a finish while retaining the exact geometry; it neither adds nor removes any locked asset or changes the revision-preservation policy.
The selected material finish does not alter the required shared peak horizon between the Hero V and É accent.
